ops.title: Under launchd nothing but SIGKILL can unpark a parked daemon — the graceful arm is unreachable
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the first real-machine E2E daemonkit has ever run. Not reachable in-process:
every existing ladder test unparks by `syscall.Kill(os.Getpid(), SIGTERM)` from inside the test.

`launchctl bootout` sends exactly ONE SIGTERM. Serve's forwarder consumes it to *start* the drain
(serve.go:186). `park` then registers a FRESH handler (serve.go:238) and waits for a signal launchd
will never send again. Observed: `serve.return` absent in every bootout wedge across three runs; the
process dies at ExitTimeOut instead.

So the park's documented "until stopped" resolves as SIGKILL 100% of the time under launchd. The
graceful arm is dead code on the production path, and the doc claims an exit that cannot happen.

The behaviour is arguably fine — the park exists to hold the flock so a successor cannot start over
half-done work, and holding it until SIGKILL achieves that. The defect is the unreachable arm plus
the claim. Same family as the four mixed-era headers: a statement that outran what the code delivers.

Related, from the same run: **D2 — the park's window is whatever the ladder under-spent.**
`Daemon.exitTimeOut()` (ensure.go:531) renders `Shutdown` as ExitTimeOut, and the ladder spends
`Shutdown`. Measured: a middle-stage (Drain) wedge leaves ~3.2s of park; a last-stage (Close) wedge
runs the ladder to ~5.1s of a 6s budget. Both die at ExitTimeOut. So the flock-retention guarantee is
bounded by `Shutdown - ladder_elapsed`, which no caller can set independently. If flock retention is
meant to be a guarantee with a duration, ExitTimeOut needs to be settable apart from Shutdown.

ops.text: The park's exit conditions in code and godoc match what launchd actually does
Either the second-signal arm is reachable in production, or it is deleted and the doc says the park ends at ExitTimeOut
